hero.headline: Stuart awarded $79 million federal grant to replace century-old St. Lucie River Railroad Bridge
hero.teaser: The City of Stuart has been awarded $79 million in federal funding to replace the aging St. Lucie River Railroad Bridge as part of a $5.3 billion nationwide investment in rail safe
hero.body:
The City of Stuart has been awarded $79 million in federal funding to replace the aging St. Lucie River Railroad Bridge as part of a $5.3 billion nationwide investment in rail safety and infrastructure announced by U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy on Tuesday. The grant, part of the National Railroad Partnership Program, will fund the replacement of the 100-year-old single-track bridge with a modern double-track structure featuring dramatically improved clearances for boats and vessels navigating the Okeechobee Waterway. Florida received a total of $496 million from the program, with the Stuart bridge project representing the second-largest allocation in the state.

The new bridge will increase horizontal clearance from 50 feet to approximately 90 feet, while vertical clearance will jump from just 6.5 feet to 17.75 feet when in the closed position. These improvements will allow more than 90% of vessels to pass without requiring the bridge to open, significantly reducing delays for marine traffic on the federal navigation channel.

Congressman Brian Mast said the century-old bridge is too low, sitting at 6 feet, too narrow, and stuck in the closed position more often than it should be. He called it a daily headache for boaters and a safety risk for everyone who shares that corridor.

The bridge serves both Brightline passenger trains and Florida East Coast Railway freight operations, making it a critical piece of infrastructure for the region's transportation network.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce City Council selects former St. Lucie County attorney as interim city attorney
cards.teaser: Fort Pierce City Council voted Monday to appoint Daniel S. McIntyre as interim city attorney when Sara Hedges ends her tenure in September. McIntyre, who served as St. Lucie County
cards.body:
Fort Pierce City Council voted Monday to appoint Daniel S. McIntyre as interim city attorney when Sara Hedges ends her tenure in September. McIntyre, who served as St. Lucie County's chief legal counsel from 1985 to 2025, will negotiate salary terms with the city before assuming the role.

The council voted 4-1 to hire McIntyre after rejecting Commissioner Michael Broderick's motion to extend Hedges' contract through December 31. Mayor Linda Hudson supported Broderick's proposal, but Commissioners Chris Dzadovsky, Arnold Gaines and Curtis Johnson Jr. voted against it. The motion failed 2-3, with only Broderick voting against McIntyre's appointment.

Hedges became head of the city attorney's office in September 2023 after serving as an assistant city attorney. Her tenure became contentious in May following controversy over a wage garnishment for an unpaid credit card account owed by Johnna Morris, the city's finance director. City officials also reported friction between Hedges and City Manager Richard Chess over Chess' wish to consult outside counsel in the matter and Hedges' claim that Chess excluded her from staff employment issues.

McIntyre has 43 years of local government law experience, including three years as assistant Martin County attorney from 1982 to 1985. He holds a bachelor's degree from University of Miami and a law degree from Wake Forest School of Law. City officials said McIntyre has stepped in multiple times over the years to serve as Fort Pierce interim city attorney during vacancies. The city's Human Resources Department also offered John J. Anastasio, former counsel for Port St. Lucie Mayor JoAnn Faiella, as another candidate for the interim position.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Nuclear Plant back at full power after control rod failure prompted shutdown
cards.teaser: Florida Power & Light says Unit 1 at the St. Lucie Nuclear Power Plant is back at 100% power after being manually shut down Wednesday following an equipment issue. According to the
cards.body:
Florida Power & Light says Unit 1 at the St. Lucie Nuclear Power Plant is back at 100% power after being manually shut down Wednesday following an equipment issue. According to the Nuclear Regulatory Commission, three control rods dropped into the reactor's core, prompting crews to shut the unit down for repairs. FPL says there was no danger to the public or staff, and no customers lost power.

Forrest Blanton lives on the Indian River Lagoon in St. Lucie County, where the plant's towering concrete structures are visible across the water. He said he was relieved by how the situation was handled and praised the company's openness about the incident.

Dr. Donald Wall, a nuclear engineering professor at the University of Florida, said residents living nearby had no reason to be alarmed. Wall said staff followed correct safety procedures by shutting the reactor down and noted the plant has multiple layers of protection built in. Wall compared the decision to a driver pulling over when a check engine light comes on.

Wall pointed to an NRC report of a similar incident in November 2024, in which Unit 1 was also manually shut down after three rods dropped during rod control maintenance. He raised questions about what the two events may have in common.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie voters head to polls Tuesday for mayoral election
cards.teaser: Incumbent Mayor Shannon Martin faces challengers Steven Giordano and Eric Strazzeri in the city's mayoral race.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie residents will head to the polls Tuesday to decide who will lead the city as its next mayor. Incumbent Mayor Shannon Martin is seeking another term and faces challengers Steven Giordano and Eric Strazzeri. All three candidates spoke about their priorities for the city Monday, with issues ranging from infrastructure and public safety to government spending and quality of life.

Martin said one of her top priorities is continuing to invest in the city while protecting the quality of life residents have come to expect. Giordano said he wants to bring a different approach to city hall, with a focus on spending, transparency and adding more amenities for families. Strazzeri said fiscal responsibility is at the top of his list, along with improving roads, drainage and overall quality of life.

Polls in Port St. Lucie open Tuesday at 7 a.m.

cards.headline: Kuhio Aloy hits first two pro homers as St. Lucie Mets fall 7-3 to Jupiter
cards.teaser: Kuhio Aloy hit the first two home runs of his professional career Sunday, but the St. Lucie Mets fell 7-3 to the Jupiter Hammerheads to close out a difficult road series.
cards.body:
Kuhio Aloy hit the first two home runs of his professional career Sunday, but the St. Lucie Mets could not overcome a late surge by the Jupiter Hammerheads in a 7-3 loss at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

The defeat ended a difficult six-game series for St. Lucie, with Jupiter winning five of the six games. The Mets have now lost seven of their last eight.

Aloy, the Mets' 11th-round pick out of Arkansas, provided the offensive highlight for St. Lucie with a pair of solo home runs.

His first came in the second inning and gave the Mets a 1-0 lead. Aloy went deep again in the sixth, tying the game 2-2.

Jupiter slugger Echedry Vargas answered with another big performance of his own. Vargas hit a two-run homer off Candido Cuevas in the fourth inning to put the Hammerheads ahead 2-1.

After Aloy tied the game in the top of the sixth, Vargas responded in the bottom half with a towering solo home run off Conner Ware, putting Jupiter back in front 3-2.

It was Vargas' second multi-homer game of the series. He finished the six-game set with five home runs and now leads the Florida State League with 21 this season. Vargas is the first Hammerheads player to reach at least 20 home runs in a season since Marcell Ozuna in 2012.

Jupiter pulled away with three runs in the seventh inning. One run scored on a groundout and another came home on an error before Jeremy Almonte delivered an RBI double off Jose Guevara, stretching the Hammerheads' lead to 6-2.

The Mets attempted to rally in the ninth after Jupiter reliever Ian Medina walked four batters. Elian Peña drew a bases-loaded walk to force home a run and cut the deficit to 7-3.

Davidxon Lara then entered for Jupiter and retired John Smith III on a groundout with the tying run at the plate to end the game.

Mets starter Will Watson, who is working his way back from an oblique injury on a Minor League Baseball rehab assignment, pitched three scoreless innings.

St. Lucie finished the day at 17-30 in the second half and 50-63 overall.

The Mets are off Monday before returning home Tuesday to begin a six-game series against the Lakeland Flying Tigers at Clover Park in Port St. Lucie. First pitch for Tuesday's opener is scheduled for 6:10 p.m.

cards.headline: Stuart awarded $79 million federal grant to replace century-old St. Lucie River Railroad Bridge
cards.teaser: The City of Stuart has been awarded $79 million in federal funding to replace the aging St. Lucie River Railroad Bridge as part of a $5.3 billion nationwide investment in rail safe
cards.body:
The City of Stuart has been awarded $79 million in federal funding to replace the aging St. Lucie River Railroad Bridge as part of a $5.3 billion nationwide investment in rail safety and infrastructure announced by U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy on Tuesday. The grant, part of the National Railroad Partnership Program, will fund the replacement of the 100-year-old single-track bridge with a modern double-track structure featuring dramatically improved clearances for boats and vessels navigating the Okeechobee Waterway. Florida received a total of $496 million from the program, with the Stuart bridge project representing the second-largest allocation in the state.

 The new bridge will increase horizontal clearance from 50 feet to approximately 90 feet, while vertical clearance will jump from just 6.5 feet to 17.75 feet when in the closed position. These improvements will allow more than 90% of vessels to pass without requiring the bridge to open, significantly reducing delays for marine traffic on the federal navigation channel.

 Congressman Brian Mast said the century-old bridge is too low, sitting at 6 feet, too narrow, and stuck in the closed position more often than it should be. He called it a daily headache for boaters and a safety risk for everyone who shares that corridor.

 The bridge serves both Brightline passenger trains and Florida East Coast Railway freight operations, making it a critical piece of infrastructure for the region's transportation network.

cards.headline: Kuhio Aloy hits first two pro homers as St. Lucie Mets fall 7-3 to Jupiter
cards.teaser: Kuhio Aloy hit the first two home runs of his professional career Sunday, but the St. Lucie Mets fell 7-3 to the Jupiter Hammerheads to close out a difficult road series.
cards.body:
Kuhio Aloy hit the first two home runs of his professional career Sunday, but the St. Lucie Mets could not overcome a late surge by the Jupiter Hammerheads in a 7-3 loss at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

The defeat ended a difficult six-game series for St. Lucie, with Jupiter winning five of the six games. The Mets have now lost seven of their last eight.

Aloy, the Mets' 11th-round pick out of Arkansas, provided the offensive highlight for St. Lucie with a pair of solo home runs.

His first came in the second inning and gave the Mets a 1-0 lead. Aloy went deep again in the sixth, tying the game 2-2.

Jupiter slugger Echedry Vargas answered with another big performance of his own. Vargas hit a two-run homer off Candido Cuevas in the fourth inning to put the Hammerheads ahead 2-1.

After Aloy tied the game in the top of the sixth, Vargas responded in the bottom half with a towering solo home run off Conner Ware, putting Jupiter back in front 3-2.

It was Vargas' second multi-homer game of the series. He finished the six-game set with five home runs and now leads the Florida State League with 21 this season. Vargas is the first Hammerheads player to reach at least 20 home runs in a season since Marcell Ozuna in 2012.

Jupiter pulled away with three runs in the seventh inning. One run scored on a groundout and another came home on an error before Jeremy Almonte delivered an RBI double off Jose Guevara, stretching the Hammerheads' lead to 6-2.

The Mets attempted to rally in the ninth after Jupiter reliever Ian Medina walked four batters. Elian Peña drew a bases-loaded walk to force home a run and cut the deficit to 7-3.

Davidxon Lara then entered for Jupiter and retired John Smith III on a groundout with the tying run at the plate to end the game.

Mets starter Will Watson, who is working his way back from an oblique injury on a Minor League Baseball rehab assignment, pitched three scoreless innings.

St. Lucie finished the day at 17-30 in the second half and 50-63 overall.

The Mets are off Monday before returning home Tuesday to begin a six-game series against the Lakeland Flying Tigers at Clover Park in Port St. Lucie. First pitch for Tuesday's opener is scheduled for 6:10 p.m.

hero.headline: St. Lucie Nuclear Plant back at full power after control rod failure prompted shutdown
hero.teaser: Florida Power & Light says Unit 1 at the St. Lucie Nuclear Power Plant is back at 100% power after being manually shut down Wednesday following an equipment issue. According to the
hero.body:
Florida Power & Light says Unit 1 at the St. Lucie Nuclear Power Plant is back at 100% power after being manually shut down Wednesday following an equipment issue. According to the Nuclear Regulatory Commission, three control rods dropped into the reactor's core, prompting crews to shut the unit down for repairs. FPL says there was no danger to the public or staff, and no customers lost power.

Forrest Blanton lives on the Indian River Lagoon in St. Lucie County, where the plant's towering concrete structures are visible across the water. He said he was relieved by how the situation was handled and praised the company's openness about the incident.

Dr. Donald Wall, a nuclear engineering professor at the University of Florida, said residents living nearby had no reason to be alarmed. Wall said staff followed correct safety procedures by shutting the reactor down and noted the plant has multiple layers of protection built in. Wall compared the decision to a driver pulling over when a check engine light comes on.

Wall pointed to an NRC report of a similar incident in November 2024, in which Unit 1 was also manually shut down after three rods dropped during rod control maintenance. He raised questions about what the two events may have in common.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie voters head to polls Tuesday for mayoral election
cards.teaser: Incumbent Mayor Shannon Martin faces challengers Steven Giordano and Eric Strazzeri in the city's mayoral race.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie residents will head to the polls Tuesday to decide who will lead the city as its next mayor. Incumbent Mayor Shannon Martin is seeking another term and faces challengers Steven Giordano and Eric Strazzeri. All three candidates spoke about their priorities for the city Monday, with issues ranging from infrastructure and public safety to government spending and quality of life.

Martin said one of her top priorities is continuing to invest in the city while protecting the quality of life residents have come to expect. Giordano said he wants to bring a different approach to city hall, with a focus on spending, transparency and adding more amenities for families. Strazzeri said fiscal responsibility is at the top of his list, along with improving roads, drainage and overall quality of life.

Polls in Port St. Lucie open Tuesday at 7 a.m.
